entries.text: Morning fog hid Bellhaven's harbor, and Mira held the unlit lantern against her coat.
Ren studied the ferryman's outstretched hand. "We cannot carry our mission across the water on goodwill alone."
Mira searched her purse while the ferry rope creaked against its post.
Ren counted their coins once more, then asked the ferryman for his final price.
Mira and courier Ren left Bellhaven to carry the moon lantern to the sleeping city of Vesper. Their passage aboard the river ferry cost seven silver crowns.
The ferryman blocked the gangplank with a weathered pole.
"A guild badge is no answer," he told Ren. "Only a traveler who knows the words may board."
Mira feared the lantern's faint glow would attract the harbor watch.
Ren leaned close to the old man and spoke the phrase he had learned in the market.
The ferryman refused the usual guild greeting. Ren obtained passage only after saying the password, "the heron sleeps beneath the bridge".
Reedmarket smelled of bitter herbs and wet canvas.
"We should prepare for the road," Mira said, studying the apothecary's blue bottles.
Ren opened his satchel and moved the letters away from the fragile glass.
The apothecary wrapped their purchase in cloth before handing it across the counter.
At Reedmarket, Mira purchased twelve blue healing draughts. She entrusted all twelve to Ren, who carried them in his canvas satchel.
At Thornwood, lanterns flickered between the trees like watchful eyes.
"A guide would keep us from wandering all night," Ren said.
Mira unfolded a map whose ink had run in yesterday's rain.
A note from Sora arrived, specifying where and when the party should gather.
The forest guide Sora agreed to meet them at the west gate of Thornwood at the third evening bell. Mira marked the gate on her map.
Sora stood before the fork in the forest road, her cloak caught on a thorn.
"The shorter way is not always the kinder one," she said.
Ren could hear whispers rising from beneath the tangled roots.
Mira followed Sora's finger across the map and tied a strip of cloth to her wrist.
Sora rejected the northern path because its roots concealed hungry spirits. The party chose the eastern path marked by white ribbon.
At a ruined shrine, footprints ended abruptly in the moss.
"Someone crossed here without wishing to be seen," Sora murmured.
Mira searched the empty doorway, but the stones offered no trace.
Sora took a small bell from a velvet pouch and explained its proper use.
At the ruined shrine, Sora gave Mira a silver bell. Ringing it twice would reveal invisible footprints, while ringing it once would do nothing.
The shrine keeper emerged as Mira prepared to leave.
"Borrowed gifts remember their owners," the keeper warned.
Ren glanced at the clouds gathering beyond the shattered roof.
Mira knelt beside the shrine and made a promise before a witness.
Mira promised the shrine keeper that she would return the silver bell before the first snow. Sora witnessed the promise.
The Lantern Inn glowed warmly beyond the darkening road.
The keeper slid open a narrow hatch. "The words of the river have no power in this house."
Ren swallowed the greeting he had used at the ferry.
Mira repeated the new phrase from the inn's invitation, and the latch clicked.
At the Lantern Inn, the keeper demanded a different password: "the fox dreams above the gate". The river password was not accepted there.
Ren sat by the inn's hearth with a sealed letter in his hand.
"If we miss the captain, our journey ends at the mountains," he said.
Mira watched the keeper sort messages into a wooden rack.
The keeper accepted Ren's letter and gave a precise delivery promise.
Ren left a sealed letter for Captain Ivo with the Lantern Inn keeper. The keeper promised to deliver it at sunrise, not that evening.
Frostpass rose beyond the town walls, pale and forbidding.
"We need someone who knows the snow," Mira said.
Ren scanned the gates while the morning bells began to sound.
A uniformed traveler carrying an ice axe approached and introduced himself.
Captain Ivo met the travelers at the south gate of Frostpass at the fifth morning bell. Unlike Sora, he would guide them over the mountains.
Captain Ivo studied the mountain slopes in silence.
"Yesterday's trail may not be today's trail," he told the party.
Sora had already turned back toward the forest, leaving Mira to read Ivo's map.
Ivo pointed to a ribbon fluttering against the snow and chose their crossing.
Ivo rejected the eastern ridge because an avalanche had buried it. The party crossed Frostpass using the western ridge marked by red ribbon.
On the glacier, distant howls rose above the cracking ice.
Ren reached for Mira's shrine bell, but Ivo stopped his hand.
"Different creatures listen to different music," the captain said.
Ivo placed another bell in Ren's palm and described how to ring it.
Ivo lent Ren a brass bell for the glacier crossing. Ringing it three times would calm the ice wolves; the shrine's silver bell could not do this.
The wolves struck as Ivo stepped onto a hidden crevasse.
Mira hauled the captain back with a rope while Ren tore open his satchel.
Blue glass flashed in the snow, and the wounded captain shivered.
When the attack ended, Ren counted what remained of their medicine.
When ice wolves attacked, Ren used four of the twelve Reedmarket healing draughts to save Ivo. Eight blue draughts remained afterward.
Mirror Lake lay still beneath a sky without clouds.
The boat keeper refused silver, pointing instead to a tray of copper tokens.
"Every crossing has its own bargain," Mira said.
Ren kept the river receipt folded away as they negotiated this separate fare.
At Mirror Lake, the boat keeper charged Mira and Ren eleven copper tokens to cross. This fee was separate from the Bellhaven river ferry fare.
The drowned chapel's roof broke the lake surface like a black tooth.
Mira descended through the shallow water while Ren held the guide rope.
An instrument glimmered beneath the altar, its needle turning toward no familiar direction.
Mira brought it into the boat, and the travelers discovered its unsettling behavior.
In the drowned chapel, Mira recovered a glass compass. It pointed toward broken promises rather than north, so Ren wrapped it in black cloth.
Vesper's gate stood beneath a curtain of sleeping ivy.
The guard shook his head at both the ferry phrase and the inn phrase.
"A city has its own memory," Mira whispered to Ren.
She read the inscription on the lantern's base and addressed the guard again.
The Vesper gate guard admitted the party after Mira spoke the password, "the moon remembers every name". Neither earlier password opened this gate.
The archivist met them in a hall lined with empty portraits.
"Do not light it as you would an ordinary lamp," the archivist warned.
Ren set down a cup from the courtyard well, but Mira hesitated.
The archivist described the precise preparation the lantern required.
Vesper's archivist explained that the moon lantern must be lit with three drops of rainwater collected before dawn. Ordinary well water would extinguish it.
Deep in the archive, drawers whispered whenever Mira passed.
"The missing names are here, but not where a visitor would first look," the archivist said.
Ren watched the glass compass tremble beneath its black wrapping.
The archivist led Mira to the permitted drawer and explained how to open it.
The archivist stored the city's missing names in the seventh drawer of the east archive. Mira was permitted to open that drawer with the glass compass.
With the final night approaching, Ren prepared to leave Vesper.
"If we are separated, I will still wait," he told Mira.
She tried to smile, though the unlit lantern felt heavier than before.
Ren named a meeting place and a day she could remember without a map.
Ren promised Mira that he would return to Bellhaven on the ninth day of the Harvest Moon. He would wait beneath the old clock tower if she was delayed.
Before sunrise, Vesper's empty streets held their breath.
Mira climbed the stairs while the archivist watched from below.
The first light brushed the roofs, and Ren's footsteps faded beyond the gate.
Mira completed the journey's final task and chose where the recovered relic should remain.
Mira lit the lantern on Vesper's north tower as the sun rose. The sleeping citizens awakened, and she entrusted the glass compass to the archivist before departing.
